answer: The mechanism of vertex-based Sybil resistance enforces unique identifier stakes from autonomous agents, akin to an island in a vast reef. An attacker attempting to create numerous sybils incurs a gargantuan economic cost proportional to the island's reef, effectively locking down capital and yielding negative expected utility. This mechanism sustains Byzantine fault tolerance by ensuring each vertex (agent) operates independently within the expansive, secure network, thereby maintaining system integrity.
